home.title: Home guide
home.overview: Home gives you a quick view of recent activity, upcoming events, announcements, and notifications.
parts: The welcome area summarizes the most important counts for your day.
Upcoming events link you to the calendar for birthdays and company events.
Recent announcements and notifications show the newest items that may need attention.
actions: Open your profile to review your personal information.
Open calendar events, announcements, or notifications from their cards.
Use the sidebar to move into the full module when you need more detail.
notes: Cards only show information you have permission to see.

profile.title: Profile guide
profile.overview: Your profile is where you review your own details, leave, calendar, and assigned company information.
parts: Profile sections show personal, work, and account information.
Related cards can show your leave, inventory, calendar, or activity depending on setup.
Editable fields depend on your role and company rules.
actions: Review your own employment and contact details.
Open your profile calendar when you need your schedule.
Ask an admin or manager if protected information needs to be changed.
notes: Some profile fields are controlled by admins to keep employee records consistent.

teamMembers.title: Team Members guide
teamMembers.overview: Team Members is used to find people, create employee records, invite users, and manage active or inactive staff.
parts: Search and filters narrow the list by name, email, role, department, status, and employment type.
Invite and add buttons create access or employee records when you have permission.
The table shows key employee details and row actions for viewing or editing.
actions: Search for a person before creating a new record.
Use Invite when the person should create their own account.
Use Add Team Member when you need to create the employee record directly.
Update roles, departments, or status from the edit flow.
notes: Available actions depend on your employee permissions and scope.

organization.title: Organization guide
organization.overview: Organization shows how people and departments fit together across the company.
parts: The hierarchy view shows reporting relationships and department structure.
Search and department filters help you find a person or team.
Department settings control the structure shown here.
actions: Drag or scroll the chart to explore the hierarchy.
Search by person, department, or position.
Use settings to maintain departments and reporting lines if you have admin access.
notes: The chart is only as accurate as the departments and managers saved on employee records.

calendar.title: Calendar guide
calendar.overview: Calendar shows company events, birthdays, leave dates, and other scheduled items.
parts: The calendar grid shows events by date.
Event forms define title, time, audience, and publishing details.
Filters and navigation help move between months or views.
actions: Open an event to review its details.
Create a new event when you need to publish something to an audience.
Use calendar navigation to check past or upcoming dates.
notes: Who can see or create events depends on permissions and event audience settings.

announcements.title: Announcements guide
announcements.overview: Announcements are used for company updates, channel-based messages, comments, mentions, and pinned posts.
parts: Channels separate audiences and topics.
The feed shows recent and pinned announcements.
Composer tools create posts, comments, mentions, attachments, and channel updates.
actions: Choose a channel before posting.
Pin important messages when they should stay visible.
Mention people when they need direct attention.
Use channels settings to manage private spaces.
notes: Announcement notifications follow channel audience rules and may be in-app only depending on settings.

applicants.title: Applicants guide
applicants.overview: Applicants helps you review job applications and track each applicant through the hiring process.
parts: The list shows applicants, positions, contact details, and status.
Applicant detail pages show the submitted application information.
Status controls move applicants through review, interview, hired, or rejected states.
actions: Search and open applicants from the list.
Review application details before updating status.
Share or use the public application link when hiring is open.
notes: Applicant access is permission controlled because applications include personal information.

inventory.title: Inventory guide
inventory.overview: Inventory tracks company assets, equipment status, assignment, and item history.
parts: Overview cards summarize asset status.
The table lists model, serial number, holder, status, and actions.
Item forms capture assignment, images, notes, and lifecycle status.
actions: Create an item when new equipment is added.
Assign a holder when an item is given to someone.
Update status when an item is in stock, in use, under repair, or retired.
Open item details to review history and images.
notes: Status and holder changes can trigger notifications when configured.

leaves.title: Leaves guide
leaves.overview: Leaves manages employee time-off requests, approvals, balances, and leave policy behavior.
parts: The list shows requests, dates, type, employee, and approval status.
New leave forms collect the date range, leave type, and reason.
Approval controls are shown to users with approve permission.
actions: Create a leave request for planned time away.
Review the date range and leave type before approving.
Update status to approve, reject, or cancel according to company rules.
notes: Leave balances and unpaid leave payroll effects depend on leave settings.

payroll.title: Payroll guide
payroll.overview: Payroll shows generated payroll records and additional payments, including payment status and processing details.
parts: The records table combines payroll and additional payment rows.
Filters and search help find employees, statuses, or payment types.
Status actions move records through generated and paid states.
actions: Generate payroll when records are due.
Add one-time or recurring extra payments when needed.
Review totals before marking records as paid.
Use bulk actions carefully when changing many records.
notes: Paid or cancelled records may become locked to protect payroll history.

payrollSettings.title: Payroll Settings guide
payrollSettings.overview: Payroll Settings defines recurring salary or payment rules used when payroll is generated.
parts: Settings rows connect employees to amounts, payment type, frequency, and active dates.
The payment start date controls when a setting begins generating payroll.
Ongoing settings continue until replaced or stopped.
actions: Create a setting before generating recurring payroll for an employee.
Use start and end dates to control effective periods.
Edit settings when salary or payment rules change.
notes: Changing settings affects future generation, not already processed records unless edited directly.

expenses.title: Expenses guide
expenses.overview: Expenses tracks non-payroll company costs, recurring expense rules, and payment status.
parts: Expense rows show amount, category, schedule, and status.
Payment rows track due, paid, approved, or cancelled expense payments.
Filters help review status, date ranges, and categories.
actions: Create expenses for one-time or recurring company costs.
Generate or review due payments.
Approve and mark payments as paid when the cost is handled.
notes: Paid and cancelled expense payments may have limited editing to preserve financial history.

expenseReports.title: Expense Reports guide
expenseReports.overview: Expense Reports summarizes expenses and payments so you can review cost activity over time.
parts: Summary cards highlight totals and status breakdowns.
Charts and tables show spending by period, category, or status.
Filters control the reporting range.
actions: Choose the reporting period you want to inspect.
Compare paid, due, and cancelled amounts.
Use details to find the source expense or payment.
notes: Reports reflect the current expense data and payment statuses.

settings.title: Settings guide
settings.overview: Settings controls company-wide configuration such as company profile, roles, departments, email, notifications, cron jobs, and leave policy.
parts: The settings sidebar switches between configuration areas.
Each page has save actions for its own settings.
Admin-only pages control behavior for the whole app.
actions: Open the setting area you need from the settings sidebar.
Review changes before saving because they may affect every user.
Use test actions where available before enabling a feature.
notes: Settings are admin-only and can affect permissions, notifications, payroll, and leave behavior.

settingsCompany.title: Company Settings guide
settingsCompany.overview: Company Settings stores branding, company profile details, regional defaults, working week, holiday calendars, and enabled app languages.
parts: Branding controls the company name and logo shown in the app.
Profile fields store contact and registration details.
Regional defaults control timezone, working week, holidays, and languages.
actions: Update company identity and contact details.
Choose the timezone and working week used by scheduling features.
Enable the languages users can select in the app.
notes: English remains enabled as the default language.

settingsRoles.title: Roles & Permissions guide
settingsRoles.overview: Roles define what users can view, create, edit, approve, or manage in each part of the app.
parts: Role rows show active roles and their permission setup.
Permission groups are organized by app resource and action.
Scopes control whether access is broad or limited.
actions: Create or edit roles before assigning them to team members.
Use the smallest permission scope that still fits the role.
Deactivate roles that should no longer be assigned.
notes: Permission changes can immediately change what users can access.

settingsDepartments.title: Department Settings guide
settingsDepartments.overview: Department Settings manages the department structure used by employee records, permissions, and organization views.
parts: Department rows show active departments and their parent relationships.
Create and edit forms define names, descriptions, and hierarchy.
Inactive departments can be retained without being used for new assignments.
actions: Create departments that match your operating structure.
Assign parent departments when building a hierarchy.
Keep department names clear because they appear across the app.
notes: Department hierarchy affects scoped permissions and organization charts.

settingsEmail.title: Email Settings guide
settingsEmail.overview: Email Settings configures SMTP delivery used for notification emails.
parts: Sender fields control the From and Reply-To details.
SMTP fields define host, port, security, and authentication.
Test status shows whether the saved configuration can send email.
actions: Save SMTP details, then send a test email.
Enable delivery only after a successful test.
Leave saved secrets blank when you do not want to replace them.
notes: Email notifications only work when SMTP settings are saved, tested, and enabled.

settingsWorkflows.title: Workflows guide
settingsWorkflows.overview: Workflows controls automation rules for app events, including in-app notifications, emails, announcements, and activity logs.
parts: The workflow list shows enabled rules, triggers, actions, and recent run status.
The builder defines one trigger, optional conditions, and ordered actions.
Run history helps you see whether automation succeeded, failed, or was skipped.
actions: Create or edit workflows for the events your company wants to automate.
Use conditions to narrow when a workflow should run.
Check workflow history after saving important changes.
notes: Workflows replace notification settings as the main place to configure notification and email behavior.

settingsCron.title: Cron Jobs guide
settingsCron.overview: Cron Jobs controls scheduled background work such as birthdays, expenses, payroll generation, and notification delivery.
parts: Runtime status shows whether jobs can run.
Job cards define schedule, timezone, enabled state, and manual run actions.
Latest result information helps verify recent runs.
actions: Enable only the jobs your company uses.
Set schedules and timezone carefully.
Run a job manually after changing settings when you need immediate processing.
notes: Incorrect schedules can create late or duplicate operational work, so test changes carefully.

settingsLeaves.title: Leave Settings guide
settingsLeaves.overview: Leave Settings defines entitlement tiers, balance behavior, holidays, and unpaid leave payroll rules.
parts: Policy controls define carryover, negative balances, and working-day behavior.
Entitlement tiers define annual leave amounts by employment length.
Unpaid leave settings decide whether payroll deductions are generated.
actions: Configure policy rules before employees start requesting leave.
Create tiers that match company entitlement policy.
Review unpaid leave behavior before payroll generation.
notes: Leave setting changes can affect balances and future payroll deductions.

settingsAnnouncements.title: Announcement Settings guide
settingsAnnouncements.overview: Announcement Settings manages announcement categories or defaults used by the communication feed.
parts: Category controls define how announcements are grouped and displayed.
Visibility and membership settings affect who can read or post in spaces.
Defaults influence new announcement behavior.
actions: Create channels or categories for recurring communication topics.
Choose members carefully for private spaces.
Keep names clear so users understand where to post.
notes: Private announcement spaces should only include the intended audience.

settingsHierarchy.title: Hierarchy Settings guide
settingsHierarchy.overview: Hierarchy Settings maintains manager and reporting relationships used by the organization chart and scoped permissions.
parts: The chart or list shows manager relationships.
Employee links define who reports to whom.
Validation helps avoid broken hierarchy data.
actions: Assign managers for employees who should appear in the hierarchy.
Review the organization chart after changes.
Keep reporting lines current when teams change.
notes: Hierarchy data can affect what managers are allowed to see.

fallback.title: Page guide
fallback.overview: This guide explains the current area of the app and the main actions available on the page.
parts: Use the page title and breadcrumbs to confirm where you are.
Use visible filters, forms, tables, and buttons to work with the current records.
Use the sidebar to move to related modules.
actions: Review the page content before making changes.
Use primary buttons for create or save actions.
Check notifications and status messages after actions complete.
notes: Some actions are hidden when your role does not include the required permission.
